about: Photoshop oracle ledger: every recorded case, classified, with our measured distance (8-bit levels, CIEDE2000). Regenerate the numbers with PAGED_PHOTOSHOP_LEDGER=write; classes and notes are kept.

adjustments/identity.note: Open + save round trip: proves no colour conversion.

adjustments/posterize-4.note: Same bins (floor(c*n)/(n-1)); values sitting EXACTLY on a bin edge (k/4 in the stimulus) fall the other way in Photoshop - a tie rule, a whole level on those samples only.

adjustments/threshold-128.note: Threshold 128 maps to 128/255 on the engine's luma cut.

adjustments/levels.note: Same formula (input range, gamma, output range); Photoshop runs it through its own table, up to 2.7 levels apart.

adjustments/curves.note: Same control points; Photoshop's curve spline differs slightly from image_core::curve_lut (up to 4.2 levels mid-tone).

adjustments/exposure+1.note: Exposure is a gain on light decoded with a 2.2 power (Photoshop's); within 2 levels.

adjustments/brightness-contrast-legacy.note: Engine: c' = (c - 0.5) x contrast + 0.5 + brightness, mapped as brightness 30 -> 30/255, contrast 40 -> 1.4. Photoshop's legacy formula is not that line.

adjustments/brightness-contrast.note: Photoshop's non-legacy Brightness/Contrast is a tone curve, not the engine's linear stretch (same mapping as the legacy case).

adjustments/hue-saturation.note: adjust.hue_saturation: hue shift and saturation in HSL; raising saturation divides by (1 - ds), as Photoshop does (measured 2026-10-05).

adjustments/vibrance.note: Engine vibrance = saturation weighted by (1 - existing saturation); Photoshop's vibrance also protects skin tones. Mapped 50 -> 0.5.

adjustments/color-balance.note: Engine: tonal-range-weighted opponent offsets (+-100 -> +-1) with luminosity restore; Photoshop's tonal weighting and scale differ.

adjustments/channel-mixer.note: Percent rows map to fractions; linear, exact up to f16.

adjustments/photo-filter.note: Engine: mix(c, c x filter, density) + luminosity restore; Photoshop's gel model differs.

adjustments/black-white.note: Default six weights; the engine's hue-sector mix reproduces Photoshop.

filters/gaussian-r2.note: Separable Gaussian, sigma = Photoshop radius, the image edge repeated; Photoshop's radius-to-kernel mapping is slightly different at small radii (under 3 levels).

filters/gaussian-r5.note: Separable Gaussian, sigma = Photoshop radius, the image edge repeated.

filters/unsharp-100-r1.5.note: a + amount x (a - blur(a)) over the sigma 1.5 Gaussian; the small-radius kernel difference of gaussian-r2, amplified by the amount (about 3 levels).

filters/motion-30-r10.note: conv.motion box-averages along the angle; Photoshop's motion kernel and end weighting differ (mean 3 levels, edges larger).

filters/emboss.note: conv.emboss (angle 135, height 3) is the engine's own relief formula; Photoshop's amount/height scale differs.

filters/find-edges.note: Interior agrees (mean 0.5 level); the border row/column differs - Photoshop and the edge-clamped window treat the image edge differently.

filters/mosaic-8.note: geom.mosaic cells are averaged differently from Photoshop's (cell value and grid origin); mean 3.7 levels.

filters/median-r1.note: Photoshop median radius 1 = the engine's 3x3 rank.median3.

filters/offset-20-10-wrap.note: geom.offset with the wrap edge policy.

filters-distort/polar-rect-to-polar.note: distort.polar runs the angle counter-clockwise from 12 o'clock as Photoshop does (source x = w(1 - angle/2pi), top edge to the centre); the interior agrees (mean under 6 levels), the seam at 12 o'clock and the corners beyond the inscribed ellipse differ.

filters-distort/polar-polar-to-rect.note: The inverse of the rect-to-polar case; the seam and the far rows differ.

filters-distort/ripple-100-medium.note: distort.ripple is the engine's own two-harmonic sine displacement (wavelength 16 px medium); Photoshop's ripple pattern and amplitude scale differ.

filters-distort/ripple-300-large.note: As ripple-100-medium at the large wavelength; the amplitude difference grows with the amount.

filters-distort/zigzag-30-5-around.note: distort.zigzag's radial profile (ridge phase and falloff to the rim) is the engine's own; mean about 20 levels from Photoshop.

filters-distort/zigzag-30-5-pond.note: As zigzag-30-5-around; pond ripples combine both displacements and the difference adds up.

filters-distort/shear-bow-wrap.note: Photoshop's curve grid (0..255, one unit = width/256 px, measured: the middle row shifts 16 px for x = 32) mapped through a Catmull-Rom to the kernel's 16 offsets; Photoshop's own spline differs slightly (mean 6 levels; the wrap seam column carries the max).

filters-distort/displace-10-10-stretch-r.note: 10 % = 12.8 px at full deflection over the 8-bit map Photoshop read; agrees on the interior (mean 0.4 level), the repeated edge differs in a few pixels.

filters-render/clouds.note: STATS. Value-noise fBm (8 octaves) between black and white; Photoshop's generator differs in contrast (standard deviation) by about 34 levels.

filters-render/difference-clouds.note: STATS. |sweep - clouds|, the clouds case's contrast difference halved by the difference blend.

filters-render/fibers-16-4.note: STATS. render.fibers' own stretched noise; mean and spread within 7 levels of Photoshop's.

filters-render/lens-flare-100-zoom.note: render.lens_flare's glow, ring and ghosts are the engine's own design; Photoshop's flare differs (mean 7 levels, the core larger).

filters-render/lens-flare-150-movie.note: As lens-flare-100-zoom; the movie prime's horizontal streak differs most.

filters-stylize/solarize.note: stylize.solarize: c <= 0.5 ? c : 1 - c per channel, which is Photoshop's Solarize.

filters-stylize/trace-contour-128-lower.note: stylize.trace_contour marks the pixel on the chosen side of the level with any 4-neighbour across it; Photoshop's line placement differs (mean 21 levels: lines on different pixels, both thin).

filters-stylize/wind-right.note: 8-bit in Photoshop (the stimulus is quantised for the replay). stylize.wind's trail lengths are hashed per row; Photoshop's streaks differ in length and placement (mean 28 levels).

filters-stylize/tiles-8-10-bg.note: STATS, 8-bit in Photoshop. Tile offsets are random; the white gaps differ in area (mean 11 levels).

filters-stylize/extrude-blocks-16-20-lev.note: 8-bit in Photoshop. stylize.extrude's parallel-projection blocks are the engine's own rendering of Photoshop's perspective blocks (mean 26 levels).

filters-stylize/extrude-pyramids-16-20-l.note: 8-bit in Photoshop. Face shading of the pyramids differs (mean 39 levels).

filters-pixelate/facet.note: Facet runs gallery.kuwahara at radius 2; Photoshop's facet clumping differs at edges (mean 4 levels).

filters-pixelate/crystallize-10.note: STATS. Jittered-grid Voronoi cells, the site's colour: mean and spread within 1 level of Photoshop's.

filters-pixelate/pointillize-6.note: STATS. Dots on the white background; Photoshop covers less of the background (about 10 levels).

filters-pixelate/mezzotint-fine-dots.note: STATS. Per-channel random threshold: within 4 levels of Photoshop's statistics.

filters-pixelate/mezzotint-long-lines.note: STATS. As fine dots, with lines; within 5 levels.

filters-pixelate/color-halftone-8.note: STATS (by the replay: the screen's lattice phase is a convention). An ink screen per channel, dark dots on white, dot radius r*sqrt(2(1-v)); regional tone follows the input but runs about 33 levels apart from Photoshop's (its dot area law differs).

adjustments-ext/desaturate.note: adjust.desaturate: (max + min) / 2 per pixel, which is Photoshop's Desaturate.

adjustments-ext/equalize.note: One table for r, g and b from the rgb histogram with half the mean bin count added to every bin, read at each bin's midpoint, ends pinned (adjust_readouts::equalize_lut, then adjust.lut1d) - a rule fitted to this stimulus (32/64/193 -> 54/79/176 against Photoshop's 52/79/175).

adjustments-ext/shadows-highlights-defau.note: adjust.shadows_highlights is the engine's own local-mean tone formula at Photoshop's defaults (35/50/30, 0/50/30, +20); mean 14 levels.

adjustments-ext/shadows-highlights-stron.note: As the defaults case at strong settings; the formulas diverge further (mean 56 levels).

adjustments-ext/replace-color-red-hue60.note: Interior agrees (mean 0.4 level); the selection edge around the reds differs - Photoshop's fuzziness is measured in its own colour space, adjust.replace_color in rgb.

adjustments-ext/match-color-self-neutral.note: Reinhard transfer in Lab against the image's own statistics with the a/b means zeroed (Neutralize); Photoshop's neutralisation differs in strength (mean 15 levels).
